YOU

Design a reliable order-processing workflow using agents. Split architecture, failure recovery, and verification across specialist teams; have them delegate focused subproblems, then combine their findings into a concrete proposal with trade-offs.

AGENT

All findings are in and complete (verification confirmed its END markers; word limits held). No further team tasks are needed — here is the combined proposal, built strictly on the returned evidence.

Reliable Order-Processing Workflow — Combined Proposal
Division of work (two squads, two nested subteams, no duplication)
Team	Task	Depth used
architecture (squad)	Pipeline design, state machine, capture gates	1 → created failure-recovery subteam (budget 0, researchers only)
verification (squad)	Independent invariants, failure-mode ranking, check recipes	1 → 2 researchers + 1 budget-0 verifier (no sub-squads)

Verification explicitly confirmed zero coordination with architecture; their findings cross-check below. Both squads remain on the roster (reusable); lifecycle defaults kept them available.

The proposal

Pipeline: five stages — intake → capture → fulfillment handoff → notification — each a consumer group on its own queue with its own DLQ. Every state change writes an outbox row in the same local transaction; a relay (FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED + leases) publishes at-least-once; a sweeper re-enqueues expired claims. Orders move through an explicit state machine where each transition = one transaction containing state + idempotency record + outbox row. Idempotency keys are stage-scoped (intake:{K} → capture:{K} → handoff:{K} → notify:{K}:{channel}:{version}), bound once, never re-minted, with attempt_count in the store — never in the message.

The core principle (architecture §2): exactly-once delivery is unachievable without 2PC/XA, which couples broker availability to business transactions. Instead: at-least-once delivery + exactly-once effect, manufactured at the money edge by gates G1–G5 — the PSP key paycap:{order}:{attempt} is minted and persisted before the network call (G1); attempts increment only after resolved outcomes (G2); unknown outcomes are blocked from re-capture and triaged to CAPTURE_UNKNOWN → manual review rather than blind retry.

Failure recovery (subteam): orchestrated saga, LIFO compensation — release inventory (C2, always safe) → refund (C1, keyed saga_id + compensation_seq) → customer notice last (C3), since handoff has no inverse and post-capture failure must compensate, not retry forward. Per-stage backoff with jitter (capture: 4×, retry only after PSP inquiry proves no charge; declines are permanent). DLQ parking rules are explicit (exhausted retries, terminal errors, 3× identical failures, >24h age) with byte-exact envelopes and fresh replay_ids; the payment DLQ pages on unknown-outcome exhaustion and auto-replays only inquiry-proven no-charges.

Cross-check: verification's invariants ↔ architecture's mechanisms
Verification invariant	Architecture mechanism	Verdict
I1 at-most-once capture on retries	G1/G2 + inquiry-before-retry	Convergent
I2 no lost orders	Outbox + persist-before-ack + sweeper + terminal-state guarantee	Convergent
I3 no double shipment	handoff:{K} + transactional event_id dedup	Convergent — verification ranked the outbox crash-window duplicate #1 (near-certain, widest blast radius: fans into fulfillment and notification), which is exactly the W2 window architecture disclosed
I4 key semantics (reject-on-changed-payload, retention)	request_hash in idempotency store	Convergent; verification adds the retention-window test
I5/I6 state↔event consistency, no half-states	Saga rows + per-stage dedup	Convergent
Inverted notification dedup (#3: flag written before provider acceptance → silent permanent loss)	Only partially covered by notify-retry	Complementary add: flag notified only after confirmed provider acceptance, else retries are suppressed forever

Independent convergence on the money edge: architecture's sharpest risk (§4 — PSP key-retention and inquiry semantics are unverified external assumptions; failure degrades every gate to "page a human") matches verification's #2 (capture retry without a stable key → double charge, R2 variant B must reproduce it). Two teams, no coordination, same single point of failure.

Trade-offs, explicitly
Outbox vs 2PC: accepted dedupable duplicates (absorbed by consumer event_id dedup) in exchange for decoupled broker availability. Cost: the dedup is load-bearing — R1 must be a CI gate, not a hope.
Orchestrated saga vs choreography: central saga rows cost a coordination service but buy seq-ordered replay, audit, and deterministic compensation; LIFO ordering trades parallel compensation for correctness (notify the customer only of the true terminal outcome).
Correctness over automation at the money edge: blocking re-capture while unknown delays customers; manual review risks operator flooding during PSP incidents. Mitigation: manual-review deadline strictly inside empirically verified key retention, 7-day auth-expiry auto-void backstop, and a degraded auth-only-hold mode when inquiry confidence drops (extra auth cost/reservation latency vs double-charge risk).
Verification before launch vs velocity: the harness (workflow.* + admin.inject_fault) doesn't exist yet; all checks are specified and semantically validated but not executed against a real pipeline. Shipping without R1–R3 leaves the two "near-certain/high" failure modes unmitigated.
Launch checklist (combined)
PSP contract verification (architecture §4): empirically measure key-retention duration, inquiry-endpoint semantics, webhook-vs-status consistency; set the unknown-outcome deadline inside the shortest verified retention.
Build the fault-injection harness, then implement R1 (relay kill → dedup no-op), R2 (timeout-after-side-effect → 1 charge ID; volatile-key variant must double-charge), R3 (dedup-flag + provider 500 → exactly 1 message) as launch-blocking CI tests, plus the invariant checks I1–I6.
Add the notification-ordering rule (flag-after-acceptance) — verification's contribution to architecture's notify stage.
Pre-wire degraded auth-only mode and DLQ paging runbooks for the unknown-outcome path.

Confidence note: the design rests on one external assumption (PSP idempotency behavior) flagged independently by both teams — that is the item to retire first; everything internal is cross-checked convergent.
